classification.difficultyReason: Interpret practical ratios and use a three-row unitary-method scaffold without a bar model.

content.prompt: Solve these ratio problems without using a bar model.

inlines.text: The required staff to student ratio for an excursion is
. If 340 people attended the excursion, how many teachers were there?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2+15&=17\text{ parts}\\17\text{ parts}&=340\text{ people}\\1\text{ part}&=340\div17=20\text{ people}\\2\text{ parts}&=2\times20=40\text{ people}\end{align*}$$
There were 40 teachers.

inlines.text: The ratio of commercials to actual show time for a particular TV channel is
. How many minutes of actual show were there in 1 hour?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}1\text{ hour}&=60\text{ minutes}\\2+3&=5\text{ parts}\\5\text{ parts}&=60\text{ minutes}\\1\text{ part}&=60\div5=12\text{ minutes}\\3\text{ parts}&=3\times12=36\text{ minutes}\end{align*}$$
There were 36 minutes of actual show.

inlines.text: Walter and William have a height ratio of
. If their combined height is 285 cm, how tall is Walter?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}7+8&=15\text{ parts}\\15\text{ parts}&=285\text{ cm}\\1\text{ part}&=285\div15=19\text{ cm}\\7\text{ parts}&=7\times19=133\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Walter is 133 cm tall.

inlines.text: Trudy and Bella make 80 biscuits. If Trudy makes 3 biscuits in the time that Bella makes 2 biscuits, how many biscuits does Trudy make?

answer.worked:
Trudy : Bella $=3:2$.
$$\begin{align*}3+2&=5\text{ parts}\\5\text{ parts}&=80\text{ biscuits}\\1\text{ part}&=80\div5=16\text{ biscuits}\\3\text{ parts}&=3\times16=48\text{ biscuits}\end{align*}$$
Trudy makes 48 biscuits.
